newsitem.title: USA: Major drug gang arrested in N.Y.
newsitem.headline: Major drug gang arrested in N.Y.

text.p: Forty-eight members of a major drug gang that operated on the Lower East Side of Manhattan and in five other states were indicted on Thursday, charged with murder, drug distribution and conspiracy, prosecutors said.
The defendants were also accused of using children, some as young as 12 years old, to conduct drug sales or act as lookouts for the gang.
The gang raked in "more than $10 million a year by carving out lucrative drug sites for themselves," Manhattan District Attorney Robert Morgenthau said.
Besides operating out of four of the five New York City boroughs, the gang also did a thriving business in Virginia, Georgia, South Carolina, Florida and Connecticut, he said.

Morgenthau said the defendants belonged to a gang known as "The Champion Crew." "They are one of the most profitable, entrepreneurial and enterprising drug gangs ever prosecuted by this office," he said.
Of the 48 defendants indicted, 40 were in custody. One defendant, Nelson Trujillo, 22, who faces a life sentence if convicted, fled to Peru, he said.
At least five women were among the gangmembers arrested.

According to the indictment, the Champion Crew grossed more than $250,000 a week operating out of Alphabet City, a section of the lower East Side in Manhattan where the streets are named for the letters at the beginning of the alphabet.
Morgenthau said that the Champion Crew rewarded gang members by permitting them to set up drug "franchises" in new areas where they wanted to expand its heroin and cocaine operation.
He said that some of the heroin sold include such exotic brand names as Satisfaction, Manhattan Special, Dead Presidents, Blood Money, Poseidon, Body Bag, Be on Time and Mad Dog.
The gang changed the names of the heroin anytime a low-level member was picked up by police, prosecutors said.

Walter Arsenault, an assistant district attorney and chief of the homicide investigation unit, also said that police found $13,000 stuffed into a hollowed out Heinz Vegetarian Baked Beans can at a "mini stash house" where some gang members were arrested.
Some of the defendants face up to 225 years in prison, if convicted.
